name: Uzzi
overview: Uzzi was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the son of Jedaiah. He belonged to the priestly line descending from Aaron, serving as one of the priests mentioned in Nehemiah 12:19. His role situates him within the Levitical priesthood during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzzi means 'YHWH is [my] strength,' reflecting a theocentric meaning grounded in the Hebrew name of God. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:19, underscores reliance on divine strength rather than human might.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Uzzi as the son of Jedaiah, as stated in Nehemiah 12:19. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented for Uzzi in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Uzzi's significance lies in his identity as a descendant of Aaron within the Levitical priesthood, marking him as part of the restored priestly order after the Babylonian exile. His mention in Nehemiah 12:19 highlights the continuity of the Aaronic priesthood, which was essential for maintaining proper worship and covenant faithfulness among God's people. Uzzi represents the faithful transmission of priestly duties in the post-exilic community.
